method: Independent current producer/consumer invariant audit; executable pre-fix failures, fault injection, negative controls, native Electron and a real GPU production. Not selected to satisfy a bug quota.
countingRules: IF-A02 promotes the previously documented R815-G31 suggestion to an executable confirmed failure and fix; it is not presented as a new idea.

IF-B04 includes stale/timeout frame fallthrough in both browser commands and dubbing callbacks. BACKEND-INTEGRATION-05 adds unowned release/acquisition as the distinct root; shared fallthrough is not counted again.
Three stale suite contracts repaired during integration are excluded from productbug count.
Matrix rows, test cases, existing regressions and productbugs are distinct counts.

findings.title: Identical playback measurements suppress replacement-media publication
findings.preProof: browser-pre.log: expected two media events for source-A→source-B, got one; unchanged-source duplicate correctly stayed at one
findings.fix: Include source document/media token in media-event dedup signature
findings.regression: independent-browser-flow.test.js: media identity changes publish even when playback measurements are identical
findings.limits: Main publisher executed from production source in a controlled Node context; renderer live sites were not run

findings.title: Detached-player cleanup overwrites newer site filter/rate
findings.preProof: browser-pre.log: site blur(2px) replaced by empty filter on remove; cleanup also unconditionally reset temporary dub base rate
findings.fix: Restore only the exact filter/rate still owned by controller; discard filter baseline so reattachment reads current site style
findings.regression: independent-browser-flow.test.js detach and normal-owned cleanup cases; native detach-site-ownership-reattach
findings.limits: Real DOM and native playbackRate properties with synthetic muted video; decoding/physical sound not exercised

findings.title: Ad mute snapshot leaks from detached video to replacement video
findings.preProof: browser-pre.log: replacement video explicitly muted before replacement became unmuted after old ad video removal
findings.fix: Restore mute only on exact element that the controller muted, never fallback to selected replacement
findings.regression: independent-browser-flow.test.js ad replacement and same-element restore controls; native ad-mute-replacement
findings.limits: Synthetic ad state and video elements, not a live ad provider

findings.title: Stale or timed-out frame mutation falls through to a different player
preProof: browser-command-pre.log: stale first frame returned overall success through a second frame mutation
browser-timeout-pre.log: ETIMEDOUT first mutation allowed the next iframe mutation, although timeout does not cancel native execution
findings.fix: Return immediately for stale source; retain timeout marker and return uncertain timeout error before trying another frame
findings.regression: independent-browser-flow.test.js source-stale and timeout cases; native-frame-source-change-command with real two Chromium frames and otherMutations=0
findings.limits: Main handler extracted into controlled authorization/context harness; timeout uses deterministic rejection, not a real network-delayed play promise
findings.relatedOwner: Backend agent owns related dubService.setRate integration check; count shared routing root only once if it confirms

findings.title: Concurrent full-page captures detach one another’s CDP debugger
findings.preProof: browser-capture-native-pre.log: visible native window single capture succeeded; overlapping captures yielded one fulfilled and one target-closed rejection
findings.fix: Reference-count the shared capture debugger lease and detach only after last caller, preserving existing external/ongoing capture-hook ownership guards
findings.regression: independent-browser-flow.test.js delayed two-owner sequence; native concurrent-full-page-capture yields two fulfilled nonempty images after single positive control
findings.limits: Small synthetic document, GPU disabled; no DRM/large-page/GPU capture acceptance

findings.title: Late media-preference response overwrites newly selected tab playback rate
findings.preProof: browser-preferences-pre.log: delayed A preference result changed B rate from 2 to 1.4
findings.fix: Snapshot tab ID/generation/URL when applying preferences and check same browser context before publishing returned rate
findings.limits: Controlled renderer callback timing, not whole-app native tab switching

findings.invariant: A narration project/listen operation must not claim current text after that text changes, even when the document and selected page numbers remain the same.
findings.producerConsumer: PDF state.pages userText/translation → prepareVoice pages → book-from-reader → openProject isCurrent → voice readiness → book-listen
proof: books-before.log: edited translation during pending import and production passed old ownership checks and enabled stale narration.
books-listen-before.log: editing after preparation still issued old-project book-listen (2 calls instead of1).
findings.fix: Capture selected page text and revalidate it after async boundaries. Pass content-aware ownership to production open and retain it for subsequent listening; reject stale narration before requesting audio.
tests: tests/independent-books-flow.test.js: pending import, pending production, post-ready listen edits and current-text retry.
Fresh closed-view/late-import control leaves new view status/controls untouched and can reopen/prepare.

findings.invariant: A failed project-reference save cannot destroy the previous published audiobook or leave an unreferenced new destination as a successful publication.
findings.producerConsumer: ready chapter audio → M4B temp encoding → destination rename → project.audiobook manifest → book-open/book-audiobook
proof: books-before.log: manifest rename EIO left old destination overwritten or newly created destination present despite failed response.
findings.fix: Move the old destination to a unique sibling recovery copy until project-reference commit succeeds. On save failure restore any post-rename manifest change, restore the prior destination (or remove new destination), and release export ownership for retry. Successful cleanup errors retain the recoverable previous copy.
tests: Old/absent destination × failure before/after manifest rename: original manifest and destination restored; retry exports and reopened audiobook available.
Previously registered audiobook survives failed replacement and remains available via real book-audiobook handler.

findings.invariant: A successful portable book export must be importable by its own consumer; a rejected export must preserve the prior package.
findings.producerConsumer: book-save edits chapter text while existing speech remains → exportBooks(includeAudio) → importBooks text/audio integrity validation
proof: books-before.log: exporter did not reject stale active speech before package replacement.
findings.fix: Reject include-audio export of a chapter whose saved speech textHash does not match its current draft, with an actionable regenerate-or-text-only error before publishing. Import safety checks unchanged.
tests: Prior valid package stays byte-identical on rejected stale-audio export.
Text-only retry restores exact edited text with pending status and no misleading active audio.

findings.invariant: Exported audio cannot be published under an earlier chapter identity after the source WAV changed across awaited work.
findings.producerConsumer: chapter output digest/manual approval → duration probes → native save picker → ffmpeg encode → M4B publication/reference
proof: books-wav-source-before.log: same-size source WAV mutation during picker and during encoder both incorrectly returned success.
findings.fix: Retain exact initial source digests and validate file type/no-symlink/content after duration probing, after picker/confirmation, and after encoding before destination publication.
tests: Picker mutation prevents encoder start and preserves existing target/manifest.
During-encoding mutation rejects completed temp output and preserves existing target/manifest.

findings.problem: Dubbing installed the new final WAV before writing authoritative quality/manifest/performance/sync sidecars. A subsequent metadata OSError or KeyboardInterrupt left new audio paired with old metadata.
findings.producerConsumer: Actual altyazi_oku.main publication tail -> real WAV + JSON files -> actual review_scene.inspect reader (including Node sync-map validator). Only the external engine's write_manifest callback is supplied by the fixture; engine synthesis is not used.
findings.before: Actual publication tail replaced a 1-second WAV with a 2-second WAV; forced quality.write_text OSError/KeyboardInterrupt left all four old sidecar hashes unchanged and the WAV hash changed. Both preservation assertions failed.
findings.change: Prepare audio, optional normalization and sidecars in a same-volume owned directory. Publish all produced files using existing crash-recoverable OutputTransaction. Print the public WAV marker after commit. Immutable take files remain beside the final output, and manifest basenames remain final basenames.
findings.after: Metadata failure/cancel preserves all old hashes. Cancel after real replacements restores old bundle. Child os._exit(91) after replacements leaves prepared journal; startup recovery restores all old hashes, then retry produces valid new audio/sidecars. Actual scene reader accepts new sync/quality against real WAV.

findings.problem: Reusing an output pathname for a production without adaptive sync left the previous .sync.json attached to the new waveform.
findings.before: Successful no-sync publication retained the fixture's old speech.sync.json; absence assertion failed.
findings.change: Added OutputTransaction.stage_delete for obsolete bundle members. Dubbing removes the old sync map in the same rollback journal as audio and sidecars; deletion is restored on cancel/crash recovery.
findings.after: Successful no-sync publication removes old map; cancellation after deletion and crash recovery both restore it; adaptive positive control installs a newly valid map consumed by actual scene reader.

findings.problem: ASR resume checkpoint was deleted before output commit. Late cancellation correctly rolled output back but destroyed expensive ASR recovery data.
findings.producerConsumer: Actual transcribe with controlled faster_whisper producer -> real matching checkpoint -> actual output transaction with cancellation after replacements.
findings.before: Cancel at write:after left no done event/final output, but matching checkpoint was missing; preservation assertion failed. Earlier JSON-writer failure control already preserved it.
findings.change: Retire current/legacy checkpoint paths only after successful output commit.
findings.after: Late cancellation and writer failure preserve exact checkpoint bytes; normal success removes checkpoint.

findings.problem: An exact 0.0 word probability survived JSON export but was replaced by 1.0 through truthiness fallback when counting perf.lowConfidenceWords.
findings.before: Actual ASR output contained probability 0.0 while done.perf.lowConfidenceWords was 0 rather than 1.
findings.change: Default confidence only when probability is None; retain exact zero. Confidence thresholds and gates are unchanged.
findings.after: Actual JSON probability remains 0.0 and done performance summary counts 1 low-confidence word.

findings.scope: Parent explicitly authorized only main dubService.setRate callback plus focused test after browser-agent referral.
findings.rootClassification: Stale/timeout fallthrough is a shared root with the browser agent's browser:command finding, extended to a separately wired dubbing callback; do not count those paths as independent root causes. Release without an existing owned target and stale old-release ownership deletion are dubbing lifecycle variants.
findings.problem: Dubbing release acquired arbitrary current media when there was no cached owner. Cached-source stale/timeout responses also triggered rediscovery into other frames; successful late replies could install a stale target after tab/source navigation.
findings.producerConsumer: Actual setRate callback extracted from main -> actual probe/command scripts -> actual browser-media ranking and media-token matcher -> JSDOM video playbackRate. Real withTimeout uses a controlled shorter deadline; no stubbed command success is required.
findings.before: Five of six initial probes failed; normal ownership control passed. In the unowned-release probe, an unrelated video at 1.7 was reset to 1. Source-stale/timeout cases fell through and reported another mutation as successful. Navigation while the command reply was pending cached a stale target.
findings.change: Release acts only on an existing matching ownership record. A chosen frame remains the only mutation target; stale or uncertain outcomes never trigger another acquisition. Retain provisional ownership on timeout for cleanup of that exact frame. Validate captured generation/view/media identity after await and delete only the same ownership object; an old stale release cannot delete a newer session's owner.
findings.after: Nine new callback/controller cases pass: stale cached release, no-owner release, cached timeout with exact-owner cleanup, fresh probe/command source change, successful rate/release, navigation before reply, stale old release preserving new owner, first-acquisition timeout cleanup, and actual multi-frame ranking selecting exactly one frame. Existing dubbing audio/client and service compatibility files also pass.
findings.limitations: Actual Electron process/frame scheduling is not exercised; callback, matcher, ranker and DOM rate mutations are real. A timeout does not cancel an already submitted frame script; its exact owner is retained for cleanup, and controller's existing watchdog remains unchanged. No GPU or acoustic quality claim.

findings.problem: Assistant preference save/undo failure leaves UI inconsistent with saved preferences or drops unrelated newer human edits.
findings.fix: Shared per-field owned rollback for set and undo, retryable undo state, explicit rollback-save failure and guarded concurrent operations.

findings.problem: Native assistant seek/speed/volume actions report completed even when their native IPC receipt is rejected or pending.
findings.priorSuggestion: R815-G31 supplied the general receipt idea; this is executable confirmation of the current consumer failure, not a new idea.
findings.beforeEvidence: native-assistant-before.log:4failed assertions after fixing an invalid initial fixture
findings.fix: Use and await the existing NativePlayerUI.command receipt for native actions; reject error and stale ownership instead of optimistic DOM setter success.

remaining: R815-B63 cross-origin audio restoration remains unresolved; no claim of universal YouTube playback/adblock recovery.
No live provider selection/translation quality, real-site login/DRM/Cloudflare, physical MPV/audio hardware, subjective listening, or long-session soak proof in this delivery.
M4B handled-failure rollback tested; cross-file process-kill/power-loss recovery is not newly implemented or claimed.
Crash during pre-publication dubbing staging may leave an owned temporary directory; concurrent independent CLI publishers not covered.
